Module 1

Meet Microsoft Copilot

One minute on what Copilot actually is — then where to open it. A frontier AI model is only the engine; what makes Copilot Copilot is the grounding wrapped around that engine and the surfaces it shows up in.

SourceMicrosoft Copilot overview — Microsoft LearnModule 1 · 1 of 7Slide 8
1.2 What is AI? — from rules to generative AI

AI didn’t arrive overnight. Each step up the staircase changed who does the thinking: first people wrote every rule, then machines learned the rules from data, and now machines can create. Select a step — or Climb — to explore, then try the quiz. Every step still matters: an Excel formula is often the right tool.

People write the rulesMachines learn the rules from dataMachines create
Step 1 · 1950sLogic rules

A person writes every rule as if … then …, or as a decision tree of yes/no questions. Predictable and easy to explain — but it only knows what someone wrote down.

In energy & at work

Safety interlock: if pressure is above the limit, close the valve.

People write the rules
Step 2 · 1980sExcel formulas

Formulas such as IF, VLOOKUP and SUM put rules and math in everyone’s hands. Still rules a person writes — just faster, and for millions of users.

In energy & at work

=IF(stock<min,"Reorder","OK") — a stock sheet that flags what to reorder.

People write the rules
Step 3 · StatisticsLinear models

Draw the best straight line through past data and extend it to predict the next value. The first step where the data, not a person, sets the numbers.

In energy & at work

Fuel-demand forecast: demand rises with economic growth — what Excel’s TREND and FORECAST do.

Data sets the numbers
Step 4 · 1990sMachine learning

Show the computer many past examples and it finds the pattern itself — no one writes the rule. Great at predicting, classifying and spotting anomalies.

In energy & at work

Predictive maintenance: which pumps are likely to fail next month, learned from years of sensor history.

Machines learn the rules
Step 5 · 2010sDeep learning

Neural networks with many layers learn from huge amounts of data, so they can handle messy inputs — images, sound and free text.

In energy & at work

Spot corrosion in drone photos of a pipeline; turn speech into live captions in a Teams meeting.

Machines learn the rules
Step 6 · 2020sGenerative AI

Large language models learn language from vast amounts of text, then create something new — answer, draft, summarize, reason — when you simply ask in your own words.

In energy & at work

Draft the minutes from a meeting transcript; summarize a 900-page annual report. This is Copilot.

Machines create
Which step is it? · 1 of 6

Click the step on the staircase you think this is.

Score 0 / 6

1.3 Where to access it — three front doors

There are three ways to reach Copilot. Two are available to everyone with a Microsoft 365 sign-in; the third — Copilot working directly inside your documents — depends on your license label (see 1.4).

New name — Microsoft 365 Copilot is now Microsoft Copilot. Announced August 13, 2026 and rolling out from August 18, 2026 (mobile and web) and mid-September 2026 (Windows and Mac), with the web address moving to copilot.cloud.microsoft. Official announcement · Microsoft Support

1 · Web Browser

Go to copilot.cloud.microsoft (shortcut: m365copilot.com) in any browser, sign in with your work account, and start chatting — nothing to install.

Copilot Chat (Basic) Microsoft Copilot (Premium)

2 · Copilot app

The Copilot app, pinned in Teams and available on Windows and mobile for Copilot on the go.

Copilot Chat (Basic) Microsoft Copilot (Premium)

3 · Inside Office Apps

Copilot appears directly in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote — working on the file in front of you.

Copilot Chat (Basic) · standard access Microsoft Copilot (Premium)

Which one should I use? Start in the browser or the Copilot app for chatting, catching up and asking questions across your work — both are included with your sign-in. Use Copilot inside the Office apps when you want it to act on the document, spreadsheet, deck or email you're actively working on — full, priority access comes with Microsoft Copilot (Premium); some organizations also give Copilot Chat (Basic) users standard access.

1.4 Copilot licensing — Basic, Premium (USL) and Copilot Credits (UBB)

Microsoft splits AI work in two. Everyday AI — summarizing, drafting, analysis — is covered by a fixed-price, per-user license (USL). Advanced AI — long-running agentic work and the newest frontier models — runs on usage-based billing (UBB) and consumes Copilot Credits.

IncludedCopilot Chat (Basic)With an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription — no add-on

Module 2

Copilot Fundamentals & Safe Use

Two things make Copilot safe and predictable at work: it's protected by the enterprise controls your organization already uses, and it grounds every answer in sources you choose. This module covers the fundamentals you'll lean on in every later lesson.

SourceMicrosoft Copilot architecture — how a prompt is processed — Microsoft LearnModule 2 · 1 of 11Slide 15
Reading / demo material — nothing to set up
2.1 Secure by design — Enterprise Data Protection (EDP)

Copilot doesn't bypass your security — it rides on top of it. Here's what's protecting you and where your data goes.

What Enterprise Data Protection gives you

On by default for anyone signed in with a work account.
  • Your data isn't used to train models. Your prompts, Copilot's responses, and the data it retrieves for grounding are never used to train the foundation models.
  • It inherits your existing protections. Copilot applies your organization's Microsoft 365 identity, security, compliance and privacy policies — including Microsoft Purview and sensitivity labels.
  • It respects permissions. Copilot can only surface content you already have access to — it never widens your reach.
  • Same protection across model providers. OpenAI and Anthropic run as Microsoft subprocessors under EDP (Anthropic is outside the EU Data Boundary). Web queries go to Bing de-identified, under Bing’s own terms.

How a prompt flows

Your data is encrypted in transit and at rest.
1 · You prompt Copilot

From Chat or inside an app.

2 · Grounding via Microsoft Graph

Retrieves only content you're allowed to see, and/or the web.

3 · Responsible AI check

Prompt and results pass automated RAI checks.

4 · LLM in the Microsoft Cloud

Processed in the service boundary — not used for training.

5 · Compliance & Purview

Responses honor your data-protection policies.

6 · Response back to you

Returned with citations to its sources.

Nothing new to configure. Copilot automatically inherits the security, compliance and privacy controls your organization already set in Microsoft 365.

SourceEnterprise data protection in Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat — Microsoft Learn · OpenAI as a subprocessor in Microsoft Online Services — Microsoft LearnModule 2 · 2 of 11Slide 16
2.2 Terms you'll hear a lot

A few names sound alike. Here's how to tell them apart.

Chat Basic & Premium

The default Copilot chat experience — the prompt box you type into. It's the same chat surface whether you're on Copilot Chat (Basic) or Microsoft Copilot (Premium).

Word / Excel / PowerPoint Agents Premium

Task-focused agents built for a specific app, opened through Microsoft Copilot or Teams. Not the same as "Edit with Copilot." On Basic: these agents need a Premium license, but Copilot Chat (Basic) users can still have files created for them via code interpreter triggered from the prompt — Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF, returned as downloads.

Edit with Copilot Premium

Assisted editing inside the file you have open — draft, rewrite or summarize what's in front of you (the ribbon button and side pane from Module 1). It can take a multi-step pass at your document, workbook or deck — the mode once called "Agent Mode."

Don't mix these up: Edit with Copilot (assisted editing in the file you have open) is different from the Word / Excel / PowerPoint Agents (app-specific agents you open from Copilot or Teams).

SourceGet started with Microsoft Copilot Chat — Microsoft SupportModule 2 · 3 of 11Slide 17
2.2 Terms you'll hear a lot · continued
More words you'll hear
Work IQ Premium

The intelligence layer that personalizes Copilot to you and your organization, grounding it in your work data. It is one of four layers of Microsoft IQ, alongside Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ.

Grounding

Giving Copilot trusted sources — the web, your files, or your work data through Work IQ — to base an answer on.

Agent

A customized version of Copilot scoped to specific instructions and knowledge for a task or role.

Agent Builder via Microsoft Copilot

The simple, no-code way to build your own agents directly inside Microsoft Copilot (covered in Module 6).

Copilot Studio

The platform for building more sophisticated agents and workflows, with connectors to the apps your company uses.

Copilot Pages Basic & Premium

A persistent, shareable canvas for working on content together with Copilot and your team.

Notebooks Basic & Premium

A project-specific space where you group content so Copilot grounds its answers in just that material. Open it from the Copilot app (Notebooks) or from OneNote. The account also needs a SharePoint or OneDrive service plan.

Create Basic & Premium

Copilot's AI design studio for generating branded images, video and graphics.

Researcher & Analyst Premium

Advanced reasoning agents — Researcher for deep, multi-step research; Analyst for data analysis.

Enterprise Data Protection (EDP) Basic & Premium

The security and privacy commitments that keep your prompts and data protected in Copilot (see the section above).

Copilot Chat (Basic)Microsoft Copilot (Premium)
2.3 Choosing your model in chat

You can choose which AI model answers your prompt. On Copilot Chat (Basic), leave it on Auto — Copilot picks the best model for the task — or choose Quick response or Think deeper. At the top of the chat, click the model selector (Auto) to see the available models.

Open the model selector to switch models for the current chat. Options include OpenAI's GPT and Anthropic's Claude — some may need to be enabled by your admin.

Prompt to use

You are a strategy analyst at Pertamina. Using publicly available sources, prepare a strategic study on the integrated-energy market to 2030. For upstream oil & gas, downstream & refining, LNG and renewables, summarize the outlook and key trends, then compare how Pertamina is positioned against PETRONAS, bp, ExxonMobil and TotalEnergies in each — strategy, latest reported performance and investment focus. Close with three implications for Pertamina, cite a source for every figure, and give it to me as a 10-slide PowerPoint deck (.pptx).

Prompt only. Copilot finds and cites public sources itself, so the quality depends on what is published and how recent it is — check the dates on every citation. Web search must be allowed by your admin. Claude models need a Premium license and may need to be enabled by your admin; on Copilot Chat (Basic), leave the model on Auto. Use Case 1b repeats the same study from the companies’ own annual reports.

Microsoft Copilot (Premium)
2.4 Work IQ on/off — web-grounded vs. Work IQ–grounded chat

There aren't two separate chats anymore. There's one chat box with a single Work IQ toggle — flip it to control what Copilot grounds its answer in.

Work IQ off

Web-grounded Chat

Copilot answers from the web and the model’s training data, plus the files you hand it — none of your Microsoft 365 data. Prompt suggestions and the / references stay web- and file-based, so every prompt starts with you finding, attaching or pasting the material first.

  • Open-web knowledge
  • Plus any files you attach — and, in Outlook and Teams, the content you have open
  • Available to Basic & Premium
Work IQ on

Work IQ–grounded Chat

On by default. Copilot also reasons over your work across Microsoft 365 — emails, chats, meetings and files — trimmed to what you already have permission to see. The context is already there before you type.

  • Everything web-grounded does
  • Your emails, chats, meetings and files
  • Permission-trimmed — nothing you can't already open
Example prompts
Without Work IQReview /RJPP Draft v1 and compare it against /RJPP Draft v2.
Suggest a reply to this subholding planning question [paste the question].
With Work IQList my meetings today and the key portfolio decisions I should make.
Recap my previous engagements with [subholding planning team] — what has been decided, and what has not?

Notice the pattern. Both prompts begin with you supplying the raw material — the documents, the pasted text. Copilot is capable, but it starts from zero every time.

The prompt gets shorter, and the question gets bigger. You stop describing the material and start asking about your actual work.

It's one chat with a single Work IQ toggle — not two separate chat experiences.

Work IQ is part of Microsoft IQ — the intelligence platform that also brings Fabric IQ (Power BI and Fabric data), Foundry IQ and Web IQ. Work IQ is adding Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Power Platform data (public preview).

Module 3

Prompting Like a Pro

A prompt is simply how you ask Copilot to do something — create, summarize, edit, transform or catch you up. Talk to it like a capable assistant: plain, clear language, with enough context to do the job well.

CreateSummarizeEditTransformCatch upLearn
SourceGet started writing prompts in Microsoft Copilot — Microsoft SupportModule 3 · 1 of 7Slide 26
3.1 The four prompt ingredients

The strongest prompts include four things — Goal, Context, Source and Expectations.

Click an ingredient card above to add its part of the prompt here — click it again to take it out. Generate 3–5 bullet points to prepare me for a meeting with Partner X about our joint study on a new renewables venture. Focus on email and Teams chats since June. Use simple language so I can get up to speed quickly.
Goal Context Source Expectations
SourceGet started writing prompts in Microsoft Copilot — Microsoft SupportModule 3 · 2 of 7Slide 27
3.2 From vague to valuable

The same task — preparing for a Strategy Analyst interview — gets stronger as you add ingredients.

More context → better answer
Goodthe task

"Help me prepare for an upcoming candidate interview for a new Strategy Analyst role in our Strategy department by creating a list of questions."

Better+ who you are+ why it matters

"I'm an HR Manager preparing for a candidate interview for our new Strategy Analyst role in Strategy. Please prepare a list of appropriate questions so I look prepared during the interview."

Best+ your sources+ the output you expect

"I'm an HR Manager preparing for a candidate interview for our new Strategy Analyst role in Strategy. Please review the candidate's resume here: /[resume] and the position detail here: /[position doc] and give me a comprehensive list of questions to assess the candidate's fit for the position."

Before you hit send, think about what you’ll actually do with the output — ask Copilot for the bigger job, then keep the conversation going, just like working with a colleague.

3.4 Prompting Tips · continued
Fun fact! — ask for the output format you want

Copilot doesn't only answer in chat — you can ask it to deliver the result as a ready-to-edit file in the format you need. Just name the format in your prompt and Copilot builds the document, deck, workbook or page for you.

Summarize this energy-outlook report as a Word document (.docx).
Turn these portfolio review meeting notes into a PowerPoint deck (.pptx).
Put these RKAP figures into an Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx).
Give me this investment checklist as a single self-contained HTML page (.html).

Name the format and the structure you want — headings, a summary table, a 10-slide deck — and Copilot generates the file ready for you to refine.

Power move! — let Copilot act in your other apps

Copilot, grounded in Work IQ (part of Microsoft IQ), doesn't only read across your Microsoft 365 — it can also act. Ask Copilot Chat to draft an email, set up a meeting or post to Teams and it does the work, asking for your approval before it sends, posts, changes your calendar or shares content. Multi-step actions in Chat are rolling out through the Frontier program for users with a Microsoft Copilot license.

Draft an email — "Send the summary above to the VP of Strategy" — Copilot drafts it and asks before sending.
Schedule a meeting — "Find 30 minutes with the portfolio team next week and send the invite."
Reply in place — "Reply to the last email accepting the portfolio review and proposing Thursday."
Post to Teams — "Send these action items to our Corporate Strategy channel."

Copilot drafts the email, meeting or post in the chat — you review it and approve before anything is sent, posted or scheduled. The action runs in Outlook, your calendar or Teams.

Prompt to use

You are a strategy analyst at Pertamina. Using the five attached annual reports — Pertamina, PETRONAS, bp, ExxonMobil and TotalEnergies — prepare a strategic study: for upstream oil & gas, downstream & refining, LNG and renewables, compare how Pertamina is positioned against each peer — strategy, reported performance and investment focus — and close with three implications for Pertamina. Then check each company against its current public status on the web — latest results, announcements and strategy changes since its report — and flag anything that has changed. Give me the study as text here in the chat, and also as a 10-slide PowerPoint deck (.pptx). On every slide, add a footer naming where its data comes from — the annual report and page for internal data, or the link to the web source for anything external.

Reports vs. the live web. An annual report is a snapshot at its reporting date; the web check catches newer results, deals and strategy changes. Web search must be allowed by your admin. Claude models need a Premium license and may need to be enabled by your admin; on Copilot Chat (Basic), leave the model on Auto.

4.6 Microsoft Copilot Notebooks

Microsoft Copilot Notebooks

A workspace with a fence around it. You decide what goes in; Copilot answers from that and nothing else — so the same question gives you a project answer instead of a company-wide one.

Reaches for
Only what you put in it — files, pages, meeting notes, chats and links
Trades
Breadth for focus — it won’t wander into your wider OneDrive, mail or the web
Gives you back
Answers scoped to the project — plus audio overviews and a notebook you can share

A notebook is an AI-powered workspace scoped to one piece of work. You gather the content that matters — files, Copilot Pages, meeting notes, chats and links — into a single place, and Copilot answers only from the references you added. Nothing more, nothing less: a notebook doesn’t reach into your whole OneDrive, mailbox, Teams chats or the web unless you put those references in it. Add more as the project evolves and the answers update with it.

The scope is the feature. Ask this in chat and Copilot searches everywhere you have access to; ask it here and the answer comes from these twelve things — which is exactly what you want when a project has its own truth.

Example Use Case Prompts

Beyond Q&A: set custom instructions per notebook to fix tone and format, generate an audio overview to catch up on the material hands-free, and share the notebook so your team can co-create in it.

Notebook or agent? A notebook is a scope; an agent is a role. A notebook is a container of references you curate for one project — Copilot answers only from what you put in it, and any instructions you set apply inside that notebook. An agent is a configured assistant: a name, a description, standing instructions, its own knowledge sources and capabilities, packaged so it behaves the same way on every task and shareable with colleagues. Reach for a notebook when the constant is the content; build an agent when the constant is the job. Notebooks → · Agents →

Availability & limits. Notebooks are available to Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat licensed users; the account also needs a SharePoint or OneDrive service plan. Supported references include .docx, .pptx, .xlsx, .pdf, .page, .loop, OneNote pages and notebooks, plus specific web URLs. Copilot grounds on up to 300 files per notebook — when you add a shared location such as a SharePoint site, it picks the 300 most relevant, so add a must-have file directly. Notebooks can’t generate images or charts inside the notebook, and deleting a notebook is currently permanent. Learn more →

5.2 Word, Excel & PowerPoint Agents

These three agents are installed for you by Microsoft and live in the Copilot app — open one from the Tools menu or the All agents list in the sidebar. Tell it what you need in plain language and it creates a brand-new file for you, saved straight to your OneDrive. They're different from Edit with Copilot: rather than working inside a file you already have open, they build the document, workbook or deck from your prompt.

Premium only. These agents need a paid Microsoft Copilot license — they aren’t available to Copilot Chat (Basic) users. They ground in your work content through Work IQ — the files, emails, meetings and sites you already have permission to see. They run on Anthropic models: if you can’t see or open them, your admin may not have enabled Anthropic.

One thing to know before you reach for them: these three are builders first. They are specialized in turning a prompt into a finished file — a document, a deck, a workbook — and the Excel Agent will also analyze the data it builds from, producing charts and year-to-date summaries. When the job is deep analysis of a dataset rather than producing a file, reach for the Analyst agent below.

Word Agent

A finished document from a brief — reports, proposals, policies, briefing notes. Give it the audience and the length.

PowerPoint Agent

A designed deck from a prompt or a source document — it drafts the slides, organizes the flow and applies the design.

Excel Agent

A working spreadsheet from a description — it builds the table, adds the formulas and sets up the structure.

5.3 Researcher & Analyst
Reaches for
The open web and your work content — files, emails, meetings, chats
Trades
Speed for depth — minutes of multi-step reasoning, not a one-shot reply
Gives you back
A structured, source-cited report you can verify claim by claim

Researcher

The agent you hand a question you can’t answer in one search — it goes away, reads widely, and comes back with a brief you could put in front of your leadership.

Researcher is built for depth over speed. It reasons through a question across several steps, drawing on both the web and your work content — files, emails, meetings and chats you have permission to see — and returns a comprehensive, source-cited report rather than a chat answer. It deliberately takes longer than a normal reply because it is doing multi-step analysis, checking as it goes, and assembling citations you can verify. Use it when the cost of being wrong is high and you need to show your working: a market landscape, a competitor picture, a decision brief. Give it a clear scope and say whether it should look at your work content, the web, or both.

Before you run it. Researcher allows up to 25 queries per user per month — save it for high-stakes questions. Simple queries finish in under five minutes; highly complex ones take 10 to 45 minutes. Choose the model and mode in the model picker at the top right (with @Researcher in a normal chat, it defaults to Auto).

Every claim carries its source, so the first thing you do with a Researcher report is spot-check it — not retype it.

Analyst

A data scientist you can hand a messy export to — it works the numbers step by step, shows the code it ran, and tells you what the data is actually saying.

Analyst works like a data scientist on your team. It reasons through a dataset step by step — and runs Python when a question calls for it — to surface trends, comparisons and anomalies, then explains its thinking and shows the visuals behind it. You can watch the code it runs and check its work, which is the point: the answer comes with its reasoning attached. Reach for it when the question is bigger than a formula — segments, correlations, forecasts, or “what is actually going on in this export?” — and hand it the file rather than a description of the file.

5.4 Cowork · continued

How it’s designed. Cowork is a prebuilt, autonomous agentic system that takes action, not just chats. Grounded in your emails, meetings, chats, files and data via Work IQ, it works through a multi-step job across Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Where Copilot Chat answers in a single turn, Cowork works over minutes to hours — asking for your approval before sensitive actions, running in a secure, isolated environment, and acting only within your own permissions. Getting access takes two things, not one: an active Microsoft Copilot license and usage-based (Cowork) billing enabled — the spending policy is an access control, not just a budget. Without one, you’ll see Request access.

Reach for Cowork when…

  • the task is multi-step and can run largely on its own (e.g. research → draft → compile → follow-up), not a single prompt;
  • it should work over your own Microsoft 365 data (Work IQ) and take real actions — send mail, post in Teams, build docs, manage files — each behind an approval;
  • you want a ready-made agent you can extend with up to 50 custom skills and Microsoft 365 App Store plugins & connectors, rather than building one in Agent Builder or Copilot Studio;
  • it should run on a schedule — recurring prompts such as a daily briefing or a follow-up sweep;
  • the work stays within one person’s identity and permissions, with you reviewing the result.
Where Cowork runs, how approvals work, and what else it can do
Where it runsYour browser at copilot.cloud.microsoft, the Copilot desktop app for Windows and macOS, the Copilot mobile app, and Outlook and Teams. You need a Microsoft Copilot license and a spending policy — without one, you’ll see Request access.
ApprovalsCowork asks before sensitive actions. Approve once, use Approve All when several are waiting, or skip similar prompts for the rest of the session. Review or revoke these choices under Permissions in the side panel; automated tasks can be pre-authorized when you create them.
What else it can doEdit an existing Word, Excel or PowerPoint file in OneDrive or SharePoint · start a task when a matching email or Teams message arrives · complete web tasks in Microsoft Edge on your device · generate images · run up to 25 scheduled prompts. Leave the model on Auto; reasoning effort defaults to Medium.

Coming to Chat (Frontier). Copilot Chat can also run long-running, multi-step work for users with a Microsoft Copilot license — track it in the Tasks view at the top right of the navigation pane; sensitive actions still need your approval. Cowork stays the choice for end-to-end work you delegate.

5.4 Cowork · continued
Custom skills — teach Copilot a task once

A skill is a modular capability you hand a session so it performs one specific task reliably and repeatably. It isn’t more knowledge and it isn’t another tool — it’s a packaged procedure, with the assets and scripts that procedure needs travelling alongside it. The one-line distinction worth remembering: an agent is the “who”; a skill is the “how”. Add a skill when a task must be done the same way every single time — your report format, your naming convention, your review checklist.

1 · Create it
From the Customize pageOpen Customize in Cowork and describe the task — e.g. a document format you produce every week.
By asking in chatDescribe the procedure in plain language, ask Cowork to save it as a skill, then review it.
By hand, or uploadWrite a SKILL.md — or select Upload skill for a .md, .zip or .skill file.
→
2 · The skill package — the “how”
OneDrive › Documents › Cowork › skills
SKILL.mdName and description (when to use it) + the step-by-step procedure · up to 1 MB
Companion filesTemplates, checklists, reference data, scripts · up to 20 files, 10 MB per skill
Up to 50 custom skills
→
3 · Cowork uses it
Discovered at session startA skill added mid-session loads in the next one.
Applied when the task matchesThe same procedure, every time — your format, naming or checklist.
Checked for qualityA plain-language quality report when you create, update or validate it.

Where they live, and when they load. Custom skills are stored as SKILL.md files in your OneDrive at /Documents/Cowork/skills/ — up to 50 of them. Cowork discovers your skills at the start of each session, so a skill you add mid-session isn’t picked up until the next one. The same applies to plugins: removing one takes effect in the next session, never mid-flight. Skill scripts run in a temporary, isolated environment inside the Microsoft 365 service boundary, removed when the task finishes . When you create, update or validate a skill, Cowork returns a plain-language quality report — still review a new skill’s output like a colleague’s first draft. Each SKILL.md can be up to 1 MB, with up to 20 companion files (10 MB per skill); custom skills aren’t supported in Cowork on mobile. Skills you create in Copilot Chat also work in Cowork; Cowork skills appear in Chat when you share them.

Sources: Use Copilot Cowork · Copilot Cowork common questions — Microsoft Learn.

10 Cowork tips — Microsoft best practices + trainer tips

Microsoft’s Best practices for Copilot Cowork plus trainer tips for getting more value and spending credits wisely. The thread through all ten: design in Chat on Auto, then let Cowork run the finished task.

1 · Plantips 1–4
2 · Runtips 5–8
3 · Reusetips 9–10
1Be specific — rich context up front

“Email Sarah about the Q2 review tomorrow at 2 PM” beats “Send that email.” Load files and work context in one pass — up to 250,000 characters per message.

Microsoft best practice
2Right-size the request

Ask for exactly the depth you need: a quick draft is light, a six-month data analysis is heavy.

Trainer tip
3Batch related work

Fold related asks into one well-scoped session so the loaded context is reused instead of rebuilt.

Trainer tip
4Plan for complexity — design in Chat first

Heavy work takes longer; complex isn’t broken. Retry only if progress stops for 60 seconds or more. Shape the prompt in Chat on Auto (no Copilot Credits), then run it in Cowork.

Microsoft best practice

Module 6

Build Your Own Agent — Agents, Agent Builder & Copilot Studio

When you chat with Microsoft Copilot — or use one of its built-in, first-party agents — you're prompting: typing what you want, each time. An agent turns that around. Instead of prompting, you save your prompt as the agent's instructions, so it works that way every time.

SourceAgents overview — Microsoft Copilot Studio — Microsoft LearnModule 6 · 1 of 14Slide 55

This module goes in three steps: what an agent actually is (and what a harness is), how to build one with no code in Agent Builder, how to package repeatable work as skills, and when to graduate to Copilot Studio.

From prompting to building

Everything so far has been you typing what you want. An agent is that prompt made permanent — written once as instructions, pointed at the right knowledge, and handed to whoever needs it.

1
Know what you’re choosing

Agent = model + harness. The harness decides what your design can even express.

2
Build it, no code

Agent Builder inside Microsoft Copilot: instructions, knowledge, prompts, share.

3
Package what repeats

Skills turn a procedure you keep re-explaining into a module the agent reaches for.

4
Graduate when it’s time

Copilot Studio when you hit the walls — memory, loops, transactions, outside reach.

SourceAgents overview — Microsoft Copilot Studio — Microsoft LearnModule 6 · 2 of 14Slide 56
6.1 Agents & harnesses — what you're actually choosing

An LLM on its own is not an agent: it generates text and stops. What turns it into something that performs work is the harness — the runtime scaffolding around the model. The harness decides when to call the model, what to send it, how to read what comes back, and which tool to call next. It also manages conversation state and context, applies approval policies, and keeps a multi-step task moving.

Agent = LLM + harness. Notice what that means: neither term is something you write. You select a model and you select a harness. What you author is the third thing — the design layer — and it has three components: instructions, knowledge, and tools & skills. The design layer is built around the harness, never independently of it.

Anatomy of an agent

You select the model and the harness — Copilot chat, Standard or GitHub Copilot; you author the design layer — instructions, knowledge, and tools & skills. The harness decides which of the three you can express and how richly, so choose the harness first, then design into it.

6.1 Agents & harnesses — what you're actually choosing · continued

The harness you pick is inherited, not negotiated: instruction ceilings, whether tools can be orchestrated across steps, and whether knowledge is reasoned over or merely retrieved are all harness properties. Read “not a focus” as the harness won’t do it for you rather than impossible — on the standard harness, files are a wiring job you author; on the GitHub Copilot harness they are a capability you inherit.

The planning rule. Choose the least capable harness that still clears the requirement, then design instructions, knowledge and tools to fit it. Capability you don't need is cost, governance surface and latency that you do pay for.

Common mistake — blaming the model for what the harness owns. “The agent forgot what we discussed” is a state-and-context problem. “It stopped after one step” is an orchestration-loop problem. “It couldn't produce the Excel file” is a harness-capability problem. Swapping the model fixes none of these.

Update — Customer Conversation harness (preview)

Microsoft Learn now also lists a Customer Conversation harness in Copilot Studio — built for customer-facing, contact-center-style scenarios over voice and chat. An agent built on it is called a Customer Assist Agent.

6.2 Agent Builder inside Microsoft Copilot
What you see when you open Agent Builder

Describe your agent in plain language on the left, and fine-tune it on the right under Configure.

From Plugins (or Agents & Skills before Plugins reaches your tenant), choose New agent. Chat your way to an agent on the left, or open Configure on the right and set it up field by field.

The first time you open the refreshed Configure panel, Agent Builder tells you what changed. Three things matter before you build:

  • Files you upload appear under “Uploaded files.” Up to 20 per agent.
  • Every agent can write code and create Word, Excel and PowerPoint files — on by default.
  • Every agent can generate graphics and illustrations — on by default.

Those last two mean a new agent arrives with them already switched on — the Capabilities controls are still there if you want to turn something off. Learn more about what changed →

6.3 Instructions, knowledge sources & sharing
Configuring your Agent in Agent Builder

On the Configure tab you shape the agent through five parts.

1

Instructions

Tell the agent how to behave — its tasks, tone, rules, steps and examples. This is where your prompt becomes the agent’s standing brief. (Up to 8,000 characters.)

2

Knowledge

Choose the sources the agent grounds its answers in. Premium: up to 4 public websites, SharePoint (100 files) and OneDrive (50), one SharePoint list, Teams chats and meetings (5 + 5), email, people, 20 uploaded files, Copilot connectors and Dynamics 365 / Power Apps data (admin-enabled). Basic: public websites — more with pay-as-you-go.

3

Model

Set the default response mode — Auto, Quick response or Think deeper. Users can override it with the model selector.

4

Skills & capabilities

Add Skills (preview) to specialize the agent on a task. Capabilities now arrive switched on — every new agent can write code, create Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, and generate graphics — and the controls stay available if you want to turn one off.

5

Suggested prompts

Add starter prompts (a Title and a Message) so people know how to begin with your agent.

Character limits. Name — up to 30 characters. Description — up to 1,000. Instructions — up to 8,000. Keep instructions focused; for longer or more complex logic, split it into steps or move to Copilot Studio. Learn more →

Sharing your agent
You — Can editThe owner; share edit rights with specific people
›
People & groups — Can chatUse the agent but not change it; groups can only get Can chat
›
Everyone in your org“Org-wide sharing for chat access” — admins can allow all users, specific users or groups, or no one
›
Org catalogSubmit for admin approval; approved agents appear under “Built by your org” in the Agent Store

People can add a shared agent only if they have the license its capabilities need — an agent grounded on work content won’t work for a Copilot Chat (Basic) user.

Considerations: Grounded Knowledge vs. Attached Cloud Files

Two ways to hand Copilot documents — and they behave differently. Grounded knowledge is wired into the agent at build time and finds the relevant bits across a library; attached files are added to the prompt at runtime and read thoroughly.

Grounded knowledgeknowledge source · set at build time
A library of documents

Uploaded files or SharePoint / OneDrive files, folders and sites

→
Searches for what’s relevant

Semantic search pulls the most relevant pieces — “find what’s relevant”

→
Answer optimized for relevance

Use when: searching a large library, FAQ-style questions, discovery — “which policy mentions X?”

Watch out: a vague prompt can miss content — be specific

Attached filesattached at the prompt · runtime
One to a few files

Uploaded into the chat, or picked with Attach cloud files

→
Reads them top to bottom

Copilot reads the files you point it at — “this file is the source”

→
Answer optimized for completeness

Use when: legal or policy review, exception analysis, “make sure you don’t miss anything”

Risk of missing content: low

Grounded knowledge limits · Agent Builder
  • Up to 20 knowledge files → Copilot searches their full contents; above that it retrieves the relevant parts
  • Per agent: 20 uploaded · 100 SharePoint · 50 OneDrive files
  • Uploads: 512 MB for DOC/DOCX, PDF, PPT/PPTX, TXT · 30 MB for XLS/XLSX
  • Copilot Studio differs: up to 500 files, 512 MB each (makers without a license in the tenant: SharePoint files under 7 MB) — quotas & limits

Add knowledge sources to an agent in Agent Builder — Microsoft Learn

Attached files limits · Copilot Chat
  • Upload from your device: up to 20 files per conversation, 50 MB per file
  • Attach cloud files: a single file or a whole folder from OneDrive or SharePoint
  • Within a SharePoint site: up to 10 files or pages · SharePoint lists up to 20,000 items

6.4 Skills — packaging work your agent repeats

Agent Builder gives your agent 8,000 characters of instructions. That is a real design budget, and it is the reason skills exist. A skill is a modular capability you add to an agent so it performs a specific task more reliably and repeatably — not more knowledge, and not another tool, but a packaged procedure with the assets and scripts that procedure needs travelling alongside it. An agent is the “who”; a skill is the “how”.

The anatomy of a skill

A skill is a folder: one required SKILL.md, everything else optional — uploaded to Agent Builder as one .zip, up to 3 levels deep.

quarterly-business-review/
├── SKILL.mdrequired — name, description, procedure
├── instructions/
│   ├── chart-style.mdextra guidance, loaded when needed
│   └── review-checklist.md
├── assets/
│   ├── qbr-template.pptxbranded slide template
│   ├── summary-layout.htmlreport layout
│   └── kpi-definitions.txtKPI definitions
├── reference/
│   └── fiscal-calendar.csvreference table
└── scripts/
     ├── transform_data.pysame transformation every run
     └── build_charts.pysame chart every run
RequiredInstructionsResource filesScripts
Inside SKILL.md
---
name: quarterly-business-review
description: Build the QBR deck when asked
  for a quarterly business review.
---
# Procedure
1. Run scripts/transform_data.py
2. Follow instructions/chart-style.md,
   then run scripts/build_charts.py
3. Fill assets/qbr-template.pptx
Front matter what the orchestrator reads to decide when the skill applies — load-bearing, not a label.
Body the procedure — the how, pointing to the files it needs.
1 Name + description always visible
›
2 SKILL.md loads when the task matches
›
3 Files opened, scripts run as needed
Why a skill instead of longer instructions
Optimized context

Progressive disclosure — the model loads a skill's instructions and contents only when the task needs them, so context stays focused as your skill library grows.

Scale without quality loss

Decompose complex guidance into modules: longer, more specific direction without degrading instruction-following or hitting the 8,000-character ceiling.

Reusable assets

Instructions, resources and scripts ship together as one integrable capability.

Enterprise-ready

Scripts run in a secure sandbox, sensitivity labels on skill files are retained and honored, and files are stored in tenant-scoped SharePoint Embedded containers.

Limits to design around
ItemAgent BuilderMicrosoft 365 Agents Toolkit
Max skills per agent88

Max file size25 MB per fileNo skill-level limit; app package capped at 10 MB
Max files350 files across all skills350 files across all skills
Directory depthMaximum 3Maximum 3
Reuse across agentsNot supported at this stage of the preview
Skills + embedded filesCannot be combined yet — support planned

Who can use skills. A qualifying Microsoft Copilot license or pay-as-you-go access, and your organization enrolled in the Frontier program — so Copilot Chat (Basic) users get skills only when pay-as-you-go is on. Skills aren’t available in tenants that use Microsoft Purview Information Barriers.

Does this change the harness? No. Agent Builder still produces declarative agents on the Copilot chat harness — custom skills are a new component inside the agent, not a migration to a different runtime. Skill scripts run in a sandbox with no network access, no package installation and no authenticated network calls; connectors, API plugins and MCP servers stay available to the agent through the orchestrator, but scripts can't reach them. Skills raise the ceiling of this harness — longer, more repeatable instruction sets — without moving the walls. If your requirement fails on memory, reasoning loops, transactions, file editing or external publishing, skills won't rescue it; a harness change will.

Sources: Custom skills in declarative agents (preview) · Add custom skills in Agent Builder · Write effective instructions for declarative agents — Microsoft Learn.

6.5 Copilot Studio — the maker harness, and when to graduate

Copilot Studio is where the other two harnesses live. The standard harness is the classic Copilot Studio most makers know: you author topics, prompts and paths, and the agent responds consistently to well-understood requests — an internal help desk that answers common questions and routes simple ones through a flow. The GitHub Copilot harness is the most capable option: it takes a goal, breaks it into steps, calls tools across connectors, knowledge, MCP and connected agents, adjusts when a step fails, natively creates and edits Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF, and supports skills and memory. You choose the harness when you create an agent in Copilot Studio, and usage is billed in Copilot Credits.

Stay in Agent Builder when…

One person's job, answered from knowledge you can attach or reach through Work IQ; one grounding pass plus one tool call produces a complete answer; the deliverable is a generated file; publishing is to your team.

Graduate to Copilot Studio when…

You hit the walls: memory across a task, reasoning loops, transactions against a line-of-business system, editing an existing document in place, autonomous or event-triggered runs, multi-user orchestration, or reach outside the tenant.

Reach for the lightest tool that does the job. The same three tiers that power Copilot also decide where you build an agent and what the agent you build can do — you only graduate to Copilot Studio when an agent needs Tier-3 reach.

Always check these capabilities and boundaries against the latest Microsoft Learn release every time you do solutioning.

PrototypeHarden
Tier 1Copilot Chat (Basic)Agent Builder (Basic)

Simple agents from instructions and public websites. No Work IQ.

  • Answers from instructions + the web
  • Files, SharePoint and connectors with pay-as-you-go
  • One user, person-in-the-loop
needs your work data → Premium license↗
Tier 2Microsoft Copilot (Premium)Agent Builder

No-code agents grounded on Work IQ — files, emails, chats & SharePoint.

  • Reads & acts over your own M365 data
  • Multi-step work within one identity
  • Generates documents, decks & Excel; scheduled digests
  • Person-reviewed output
needs systems, triggers or outside reach → copy to Copilot Studio↗
Tier 3Copilot StudioLow-code, IT-governed

Centrally governed agents wired into line-of-business systems via connectors and Power Automate.

  • Line-of-business system integration
  • Autonomous event-/schedule-triggered runs
  • Cross-entity / multi-user orchestration
  • External / non-tenant access (no Entra ID)
  • Choose GPT or Anthropic models

The usual path — prototype, then harden. Prove the idea fast in Agent Builder (Tier 1–2), then copy it to Copilot Studio (Tier 3) — its configuration and instructions carry over — or call it from a Copilot Studio workflow when it needs system connectors, autonomous triggers, multi-user orchestration or external reach. If a task stays within one person's identity and a human reviews the output, you usually don't need Copilot Studio at all.
